faq.q: How do I know I am getting angry?
faq.a: Your body gives clues first: a hot face, a fast heartbeat, tight fists or a loud voice. Spotting these early gives you time to calm down.

faq.q: What is flower and candle breathing?
faq.a: Breathe in slowly through your nose as if smelling a flower, then breathe out slowly through your mouth as if blowing out a candle. Do it three to five times to calm your body.
asks: How do I do calm breathing?

faq.q: Why does moving my body help?
faq.a: When you are angry, your muscles fill with energy ready for action. Jumping, stretching or walking uses that energy up, so your body can relax.

faq.q: Who can I talk to when I am angry?
faq.a: A parent or carer, a teacher, an older brother or sister, a grandparent or a school counsellor. Pick someone you trust and tell them what happened and how you feel.
asks: Who should I tell when I am upset?

faq.q: What if I already shouted or hit someone?
faq.a: Everyone makes mistakes. Calm down first, then say sorry and help fix things. Next time, try to catch the warning signs a little earlier.
asks: I lost my temper, what now?

facts: Breathing out slowly, for longer than you breathe in, helps slow your heart rate and calm your body.
Exercise helps your body use up stress chemicals such as adrenaline.

quiz.why: You breathe out slowly as if gently blowing out a candle, which calms your body.

wrong.1: Breathing in is the flower part, and it is slow too.
wrong.2: Holding your breath does not calm you; slow breathing does.
